---
title: "R8. The standards landscape"
description: "Which standards apply to your analysis, and when each one bites."
---


Which standards apply to NHSBSA analysis, and how they fit together.

Several standards govern analysis in government. They overlap, they are not all mandatory for all
work, and it is not obvious from their titles which apply to you.

This section says what each is for and, more usefully, **when it bites**.

## The short answer

::: {.callout-note title="Which applies to your work" appearance="minimal" icon=false}
<br>
**All NHSBSA analysis** follows GovS 010 and the AQuA Book.

**Official statistics** additionally follow the Code of Practice for Statistics. That is a narrower
set of outputs than "everything we publish".

**Analysis involving code** additionally follows the NHSBSA Analytical Code Assurance Playbook.

**Appraisal and evaluation** additionally follow the Green and Magenta Books.
:::

{{< include /guidance/_partials/table-standards.qmd >}}

Getting the boundary wrong is costly in both directions. Applying the full Code of Practice to a
routine internal data request wastes effort the organisation does not have. Failing to apply it to
an official statistic is a regulatory matter.

## What each of them asks for

The two that apply to everything are GovS 010 and the AQuA Book. The one that applies to
official statistics as well is the Code of Practice for Statistics.
[What each standard asks for](r9-what-each-standard-asks-for.qmd) sets out what is in each of
them, and what RIGOUR means in full.

## The ones that apply to particular work

| Standard | What it covers | When it bites |
|---|---|---|
| **NHSBSA Analytical Code Assurance Playbook** | Version control, testing, peer review, readable and modular code, documentation, open sourcing | Whenever your analysis involves code |
| **NHSBSA Data Science Playbook** | The workflow for Data Science initiatives: problem definition, assigning a critical friend, analysis, wrap up | Data Science initiatives |
| **NHSBSA Open Data Standards** | How NHSBSA publishes open data | Open data releases |
| **Green Book** | Appraisal of policies, programmes and projects: costs, benefits and risks of alternatives | Appraisal work |
| **Magenta Book** | Evaluation: assessing an intervention's design, implementation and outcomes | Evaluation work |
| **Orange Book** | Risk management principles and concepts | Assessing analytical risk. Referenced by GovS 010 section 4.2 |
| **Government Data Quality Framework** | Managing and describing data quality | Where data quality is a material concern |
| **Data and AI Ethics Framework** | Using data and AI appropriately and responsibly. Seven principles | See [ethics and transparency](r11-ethics-and-personal-data.qmd) |
| **Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard** | Publishing what an algorithmic tool does, what it rests on and who is accountable for it | Where a tool significantly influences an operational decision with public effect, or interacts with the public directly. Not for analytical models supporting broad policy-making |
| **AI Playbook for the UK Government** | Ten principles for building, buying and using AI in government | Where your analysis builds on or uses an AI system |
| **Introduction to AI assurance** (DSIT) | Assurance mechanisms for AI systems: risk assessment, algorithmic impact assessment, bias audit, compliance audit, conformity assessment, formal verification | Where an AI system has to be evaluated rather than just built |

## If your analysis uses AI or an algorithmic tool

This playbook covers analysis. It does not cover building or assuring AI systems, and you should not
read it as though it does. What it can tell you is which obligations attach.

- **The Data and AI Ethics Framework applies, in full.** Its scope was extended to AI and algorithmic
  technologies in December 2025 and its seven principles cover both. [Ethics and transparency](r11-ethics-and-personal-data.qmd)
- **The Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard may apply, and the test is narrower than it
  sounds.** NHSBSA is in scope as an organisation, but within that the standard is mandatory only for
  tools with a significant influence on a decision-making process with public effect, or which
  directly interact with the public. An analytical model supporting broad policy-making is
  deliberately outside it. NHSBSA has two records on the public register, for the Prescriptions and
  Dental Exemption check and for the Residency Checker, and those are the nearest worked examples
  there are.
  [Algorithmic transparency and AI](r12-algorithmic-transparency-and-ai.qmd) carries the test, the two roles the standard
  names, and what this playbook proposes for NHSBSA.
- **The AI Playbook's ten principles apply to the system**, and DSIT's assurance mechanisms are how
  it gets evaluated. Both are linked in [standards and further guidance](r4-standards-and-guidance.qmd).
- **An AI system can still be Business Critical**, and if it is, [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd)
  applies on top of everything above.

**The short version is that AI analysis is assured the same way as any other analysis**, plus the
transparency duties named above. This playbook signposts the AI estate rather than duplicating it. Building and assuring an AI system is a different subject with its own
guidance. A playbook that half-covers it would be worse than one that points at the guidance
covering it properly.

## How they fit together

They are layers rather than alternatives, and they rarely conflict.

GovS 010 sets the requirement. The AQuA Book explains how to meet it. The Code of Practice adds
obligations for official statistics. The code assurance playbook adds obligations where there is
code. The Green, Magenta and Orange Books add depth for particular kinds of work. The AI estate applies
on top when a system rather than an analysis is what is being assured.

**Where two sources appear to conflict, the more specific and more recent governs, and you should
raise it.** If this playbook disagrees with a standard, the standard is right and this playbook needs
fixing. Say so via the route in [who to ask](r3-who-to-ask.qmd).

## The five NHSBSA playbooks

This is one of five, and they are designed to work together rather than overlap.

| Playbook | Use it for |
|---|---|
| **Producing Quality Analysis**, this one | Planning, assuring and communicating any piece of analysis |
| [Analytical Code Assurance](https://nhsbsa-data-analytics.github.io/nhsbsa-analytical-code-assurance-playbook) | Version control, testing, peer review and documentation of analytical code |
| [Data Science](https://nhsbsa-data-analytics.github.io/nhsbsa-data-science-playbook) | The end-to-end workflow for a Data Science initiative |
| [Data Visualisation Standards](https://nhsbsa.github.io/nhsbsa-digital-playbook/data/data-visualisation/) | Charts, tables and dashboards, in the Digital, Data and Technology Playbook |
| Official Statistics | Developing, maintaining and publishing official statistics. In development |

If your work involves code, you need this playbook and the code assurance one. If it is a Data
Science initiative, the Data Science Playbook is the one that sequences your work. If it produces a
chart, a table or a dashboard, the Data Visualisation Standards say how it should look and how it
should be labelled.

## Where to find them

Every standard named here is linked from
[standards and further guidance](r4-standards-and-guidance.qmd).
